If you post on reddit on a regular basis, there's a chance you've tried to submit a link to a subreddit that someone else has already posted. When this happens, a line of text will appear that reads, “that link has already been submitted, but you can try to submit it again”. You'll then be redirected to the original post.

It doesn't matter when the original link was posted—three weeks ago, or three years ago. It also doesn't matter if it was downvoted to oblivion, removed, or caught it a spam filter. If it's been posted before, for some reason, Reddit doesn't want it posted again.

Also, although it says, “but you can try to submit it again”, as far as I can tell, there's no clear-cut way to submit it again. You'll get the same message and be redirected to the same page if you try again. This, of course, can be a bit aggravating to self-promoters, who want to share the same article more than once, or content creators who find that someone else is “karma whoring” with their material.

So, here's a work-around I've found that, as of 2015, works like a charm.

For this example, lets say we want to post this link http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/magazine-24518305 in the /r/scifi subreddit.

Except, it's already been posted.

Here's what to do: take the original link, and append a ? to the end. I also recommend adding extra characters after the ? to make sure it goes through, and so the URL looks a little more “natural”.

Here are some working examples:
http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/magazine-24518305?xVm823op
http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/magazine-24518305?-
http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/magazine-24518305?nofollow

It seems that all characters after the ? are ignored, but reddit will still recognize it as an entirely new URL. It's a win-win.

Your post should go through just fine.
